correctness.rationale: Complete general proof reduces the Tjurina quotient of separated sums to the kernel of the r-fold Kronecker sum of a square-zero Milnor-class operator. Jordan decomposition and a Clebsch–Gordan weight count give central binomial kernel dimensions. Fourier coefficient integration plus Gaussian Laplace method gives the sharp constant and O(1/r) error, with the secondary saddle at s=0 explicitly bounded; two-variable Briançon–Skoda supplies square-zero for all isolated plane-curve germs. Exact modular-matrix computations of 5 configurations corroborate finite cases, including published (16,15,2,226) and (12,11,3,1363).

evidence: Almirón Theorem 1 gives a two-summand identity with additional auxiliary invariants, and Corollary 2 simplifies when one factor is square-zero. For r greater than two the partial sum generally has larger nilpotency index, so the published two-square-zero simplification does not recursively give the displayed result using only mu and tau.
Zheng–Zuo develops filtered two-summand results whose specialization alone does not state the exact all-r count and asymptotic.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The precise infinite family law requires determining all iterated Jordan multiplicities and applying an asymptotic saddle analysis. Its individual r=2 and r=3 examples are explicitly covered and not claimed original; the general result has additional quantifiers and sharp asymptotic content. Residual risk: a general tensor-Kronecker nilpotent theorem may immediately imply this classification.

value.rationale: Natural r-fold Thom–Sebastiani tower classification for all isolated plane-curve germs, with exact ordinary Tjurina numbers and a nontrivial sharp universal inverse-square-root decay rate. It resolves the entire sequence and its asymptotic from just mu/tau rather than computing isolated r=2,3 examples. Its restrictions and reliance on classical Jordan techniques are explicitly stated.
